item.title: New details from tragic explosion: Teens held onto munition for over an hour before it exploded
item.description:
Ninth-grade students from ORT Ma’alot Yeshiva High School held a cluster munition they found during an annual school trip in the Upper Galilee for more than an hour, unaware of the danger. The munition exploded in the Mitzpe Pe'er area, killing student Elazar Yair Wilensky and injuring 23 other teenagers.
The students said that during the hike they found several pieces of military ordnance, including two missiles, and even collected some of them. According to them, they had not received a briefing or instructions on what to do if they encountered unexploded ordnance.
They also said they did not notice a sign warning of unexploded ordnance and prohibiting entry to the area.

item.title: Terror attack foiled: Four Islamic Jihad terrorists arrested in Samaria
item.description:
This week, IDF soldiers, guided by Shin Bet intelligence, conducted two arrests in the villages of Qabatiya and Arraba, during which four Islamic Jihad terrorists who were planning to carry out a terror attack in northern Samaria were apprehended.
In another apprehension this week, in the Beit Rima area, IDF soldiers apprehended a wanted individual involved in arms trafficking.
The terrorists were transferred for further questioning by the security forces.

item.title: Following tragedy in the north: Education Ministry providing emotional support to students
item.description:
The Education Ministry expressed sorrow over the death of Elazar Yair Wilensky, a ninth-grade student at the ORT Ma’alot yeshiva high school, who was killed during a school trip in northern Israel.
Teams from the Education Ministry’s psychological counseling service are providing emotional support and assistance to students, families, and educational staff in hospitals, educational institutions, and the community. At the same time, the ministry instructed schools to hold age-appropriate discussions in classrooms and identify students who may need support following the incident.

item.title: Report: Saudis stopped public alerts of Houthi strikes
item.description:
Saudi Arabia stopped issuing public warnings about Houthi attacks just days before a series of strikes on Riyadh airport that killed at least 18 people and wounded more than 300, Reuters reported.
According to the report, Saudi authorities did not explain why the public alerts were discontinued or why no warnings were issued before the four attacks that took place over the past week.
